title: Naval Communications and Telecommunications Operations Certification Practice Exam

questions.question: Which network enclave is used in the U.S. Navy to communicate specifically with friendly allies, permitting point-to-point or multipoint information transfer from unclassified up to Top Secret?
options: NIPRNET
SIPRNET
JWICS
CENTRIXS
questions.correct_answer: JWICS

questions.question: Which of the following describes the function of NIPRNET in Navy network communications?
options: A long-haul IP-based network built to support unclassified IP data communications for combat support applications
The Department of Defense's largest interoperable command and control data network supporting global command and control systems
A secure internal networking system designed strictly for tactical weapon system coordination
A satellite-based intelligence network used exclusively for sharing top secret surveillance data
questions.correct_answer: A long-haul IP-based network built to support unclassified IP data communications for combat support applications

questions.question: Which organization has the primary operational responsibility to train, certify, and provide combat-ready Navy forces to combat commands?
options: NAVIFOR
NETWARCOM
U.S. Fleet Forces Command
NCDOC
questions.correct_answer: U.S. Fleet Forces Command

questions.question: Which agency is responsible for providing operational direction to the Defense Communication Systems (DCS) supporting the Navy, Army, and Air Force?
options: Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA)
Navy Communication Security Material System (NCMS)
Navy Cyber Defense Operations Center (NCDOC)
Office of the Chief of Naval Operations (OPNAV)
questions.correct_answer: Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA)

questions.question: Which watchstander represents the highest qualified personnel at a NCTAMS, acting as the primary assistant for supervising and coordinating all telecommunication functions ashore?
options: Communications Watch Officer (CWO)
Technical Control Supervisor (TCS)
Joint Fleet Telecommunications Operations Center (JFTOC) Watch Officer
Radio Officer (RO)
questions.correct_answer: Joint Fleet Telecommunications Operations Center (JFTOC) Watch Officer

questions.question: Which supporting telecommunication command acts as the 'ISP network for the fleet' and consists of four regional entities (ECRNOC, IRNOC, PRNOC, and UARNOC)?
options: NCTAMS
NCTS
FLTNOC
NIOC
questions.correct_answer: FLTNOC

questions.question: What are the exact geographical locations of the Navy's two Computer and Telecommunications Area Master Stations (NCTAMS)?
options: San Diego, CA and Jacksonville, FL
Norfolk, VA and Pearl Harbor, HI
Virginia and Hawaii
Naples, IT and Bahrain
questions.correct_answer: Virginia and Hawaii

questions.question: How many NCTS (Naval Computer and Telecommunication Systems) locations exist to provide support when NCTAMS is down, and which are they?
options: 5 locations: Jacksonville, San Diego, Yokosuka, Guam, and Bahrain
7 locations: Jacksonville, San Diego, Far East Yokosuka, Guam, Sicily, Bahrain, and Naples
4 locations: ECRNOC, IRNOC, PRNOC, and UARNOC
6 locations: Virginia, Hawaii, Guam, Rota, Naples, and Yokosuka
questions.correct_answer: 7 locations: Jacksonville, San Diego, Far East Yokosuka, Guam, Sicily, Bahrain, and Naples

questions.question: Which command is specifically tasked with supporting Navy Information Operations (IO) and Signals Intelligence (SIGINT) operations?
options: NCDOC
NIOC
NCMS
NAVIFOR
questions.correct_answer: NIOC

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct hierarchical chain of supporting telecommunication commands, in order from highest to lowest?
options: US Fleet Forces Command -> NAVIFOR -> NETWARCOM -> NCDOC -> NCMS -> NCTAMS -> NCTS -> NIOC -> FLTNOC
NAVIFOR -> US Fleet Forces Command -> NETWARCOM -> NCMS -> NCDOC -> NCTS -> NCTAMS -> FLTNOC -> NIOC
US Fleet Forces Command -> NETWARCOM -> NAVIFOR -> NCMS -> NCDOC -> NCTAMS -> NCTS -> FLTNOC -> NIOC
NETWARCOM -> US Fleet Forces Command -> NAVIFOR -> NCDOC -> NCMS -> NCTS -> NCTAMS -> NIOC -> FLTNOC
questions.correct_answer: US Fleet Forces Command -> NAVIFOR -> NETWARCOM -> NCDOC -> NCMS -> NCTAMS -> NCTS -> NIOC -> FLTNOC

questions.question: Which shipboard officer is responsible for the organization, supervision, and coordination of the command's exterior communications, typically holding a rate of O-1 or above and reporting to the CO?
options: Radio Officer (RO)
Communications Watch Officer (CWO)
Communications Officer (COMMO)
Technical Control Supervisor (TCS)
questions.correct_answer: Communications Officer (COMMO)

questions.question: What is the primary responsibility of the ship's Radio Officer (RO) regarding watchstanding and operations?
options: Direct tactical employment of weapon systems in the Combat Information Center
Overall command and physical security of the entire naval station
In charge of the communication system, preparing the watch bill, maintaining the station bill, and preparing SOPs
Direct physical custody and auditing of all unclassified message traffic
questions.correct_answer: In charge of the communication system, preparing the watch bill, maintaining the station bill, and preparing SOPs

questions.question: Which watchstander is a highly qualified enlisted Sailor (typically E-4 to E-6) responsible for incoming and outgoing traffic, ensuring all messages are transmitted and received properly?
options: Technical Control Supervisor (TCS)
Communications Watch Officer (CWO)
Radio Officer (RO)
CMS Custodian
questions.correct_answer: Communications Watch Officer (CWO)

questions.question: What is the primary role of the Technical Control Supervisor (TCS) on watch?
options: Acts as the direct representative of the Commanding Officer for all shipboard maintenance
Responsible for the physical security and stowage of cryptographic publications
Establishment and maintenance of required circuits, and initiating action to restore or bypass failed equipment
Releasing naval messages in the name of the command
questions.correct_answer: Establishment and maintenance of required circuits, and initiating action to restore or bypass failed equipment

questions.question: What inventory procedure is strictly required prior to assuming a watch when dealing with Top Secret (TS) level cryptographic materials?
options: Single-person visual confirmation logged electronically
Two Person Inventory (TPI) with a witness
Weekly audit by the Technical Control Supervisor
Direct verbal sign-off from the Commanding Officer
questions.correct_answer: Two Person Inventory (TPI) with a witness

questions.question: Which of the following is a strict rule regarding the maintenance of the Master Station Log (MSL)?
options: Erase mistakes cleanly using corrected fluid or administrative tape
No erasing is allowed; mistakes must be corrected using a single-line strikeout
Logs must be shredded immediately after watch turnover to preserve secrecy
Only the Commanding Officer is authorized to make corrections to the log
questions.correct_answer: No erasing is allowed; mistakes must be corrected using a single-line strikeout

questions.question: Under what condition are naval messages restricted to 100-200 words, and what is the primary purpose of this restriction?
options: Minimize Conditions; initiated to conserve bandwidth and avoid suspicion
EMCON Conditions; initiated to prevent radio frequency detection by the enemy
CRITIC Conditions; initiated to speed up transmission of highly sensitive information
DAMA Conditions; initiated to allow multiple units to share a single satellite channel
questions.correct_answer: Minimize Conditions; initiated to conserve bandwidth and avoid suspicion

questions.question: Which naval message type is the most widely used by the Department of Defense (DoD), capable of handling information from unclassified up to Top Secret?
options: Defense Special Security Communication System (DSSCS)
General Service Messages (GENSER)
CRITIC Messages
COMMSPOT Reports
questions.correct_answer: General Service Messages (GENSER)

questions.question: What is a 'CRITIC' message, and what format does it utilize?
options: A highly detailed engineering report that uses standard GENSER format
A short, concise, highest priority message using a modified SI format to report critical facts directly to senior government decision-makers
A message used to notify adjacent ships that personnel are working aloft
A unclassified administrative notification concerning change of command
questions.correct_answer: A short, concise, highest priority message using a modified SI format to report critical facts directly to senior government decision-makers

questions.question: In naval message drafting, who is authorized to release messages for transmission in the name of the command or activity?
options: The Drafter
The Originator
The Releaser
The Technical Control Supervisor
questions.correct_answer: The Releaser

questions.question: Which special handling marking is applied to certain unclassified messages that have potential value but do not meet the strict requirements of a security classification?
options: Restricted Data (RD)
Formerly Restricted Data (FRD)
For Official Use Only (FOUO)
Encrypted For Transmission Only (EFTO)
questions.correct_answer: Encrypted For Transmission Only (EFTO)

questions.question: What type of report must be sent to advise of any situation that might cause significant disruption in communications?
options: COMMSHIFT
COMMSPOT
COMSPOT
NAVMACS
questions.correct_answer: COMMSPOT

questions.question: In naval messaging, what does an Address Indicator Group (AIG) represent?
options: A single plain language address used for local routing within a ship
A collection of 16 or more plain language addresses that frequently occur as a group
A collection of 4 or more PLAs sharing an operational or administrative chain of command
The unique cryptographic key used to encrypt tactical messages
questions.correct_answer: A collection of 16 or more plain language addresses that frequently occur as a group

questions.question: What is a Collective Address Designator (CAD) in naval communication routing?
options: A group of 16 or more PLAs used for global message distribution
The plain language address of the Officer in Tactical Command
A collection of 4 or more PLAs that share an operational or administrative chain of command
A routing signal used by maritime and allied services under ACP 131
questions.correct_answer: A collection of 4 or more PLAs that share an operational or administrative chain of command

questions.question: Under ACP 131, what are Q and Z signals used for?
options: To encrypt classified data before transmission
To serve as operating signals used by maritime and allied military services
To indicate the priority of message routing
To identify the geographical boundaries of FLTNOC regions
questions.correct_answer: To serve as operating signals used by maritime and allied military services

questions.question: What is the direct biological cause of muscle spasms during an electrical shock?
options: Voltage differential between the hands
Electric current passing through the body
Thermal energy generated by contact resistance
Magnetic fields surrounding high-voltage wires
questions.correct_answer: Electric current passing through the body

questions.question: What is the #1 cause of death from electrical shock?
options: Severe external burns
Ventricular fibrillation (disorganized heart rhythm)
Suffocation from respiratory muscle paralysis
Rapid drop in blood pressure
questions.correct_answer: Ventricular fibrillation (disorganized heart rhythm)

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct sequence of actions to take if you suspect a fellow Sailor has suffered an electric shock?
options: Immediately pull the victim away with your hands, administer CPR, then secure the power
Turn off the electrical power source, protect yourself with dry insulating material, do NOT touch the victim directly, and call for emergency medical assistance
Call the medical team first, check the victim's pulse, then use a wet cloth to cool their skin
Report the hazard to the safety officer, verify the tag-out logs, and wait for the power to automatically cycle
questions.correct_answer: Turn off the electrical power source, protect yourself with dry insulating material, do NOT touch the victim directly, and call for emergency medical assistance

questions.question: What is the mathematical formula used to determine the severity of an electrical shock?
options: CURRENT + PATH + RESISTANCE + TIME
VOLTAGE x CURRENT x TIME
CURRENT x RESISTANCE / TIME
VOLTAGE + PATH + RESISTANCE + CURRENT
questions.correct_answer: CURRENT + PATH + RESISTANCE + TIME

questions.question: How does wet or damaged skin affect the severity of an electrical shock?
options: It increases skin resistance, reducing current flow
It reduces skin resistance, allowing greater current flow and increasing the risk of severe shock
It has no measurable effect on electrical shock severity
It prevents ventricular fibrillation by dissipating the electrical charge
questions.correct_answer: It reduces skin resistance, allowing greater current flow and increasing the risk of severe shock

questions.question: Under RADHAZ guidelines, what does HERP stand for, and what are its primary biological concerns?
options: Hazardous Electromagnetic Radiation to Personnel; concerns whole-body or localized temperature increases and RF burns
High Energy Radio Propagation; concerns long-distance signal attenuation
Hazardous Emission of Radar Particles; concerns respiratory damage from breathing ionized air
Hearing Emergency Response Protocol; concerns ear drum damage from loud transmitters
questions.correct_answer: Hazardous Electromagnetic Radiation to Personnel; concerns whole-body or localized temperature increases and RF burns

questions.question: What is the concern of Hazards of Electromagnetic Radiation to Ordnance (HERO)?
options: The ignition of fuel-air mixtures during aircraft fueling operations
Electromagnetic radiation inducing currents large enough to prematurely fire or damage electrically initiated ordnance
Thermal damage to personnel handling metallic missile launchers
Interference with shipboard networks caused by high-power radar emissions
questions.correct_answer: Electromagnetic radiation inducing currents large enough to prematurely fire or damage electrically initiated ordnance

questions.question: What is the best practice to establish a safe environment for HERO during operations?
options: Route all ordnance through unsecure passageways
De-energize equipment or set transmitters and transceivers to the 'Standby' position
Increase transmitter power to push signals past the ordnance
Use only manual tag-out systems on the launch computers
questions.correct_answer: De-energize equipment or set transmitters and transceivers to the 'Standby' position

questions.question: Under Hazards of Electromagnetic Radiation to Fuel (HERF), what is the minimum spark gap figure noted for the potential ignition of a fuel-air mixture?
options: Approximately 0.1 mm (0.004 inches)
Approximately 0.5 mm (0.02 inches)
Approximately 1.0 mm (0.04 inches)
Approximately 2.0 mm (0.08 inches)
questions.correct_answer: Approximately 0.5 mm (0.02 inches)

questions.question: What is the function of a Type 1 RADHAZ warning sign?
options: Excludes personnel from proceeding past a designated point without command authority
Advises personnel of an RF hazard at the boundary of the Permissible Exposure Limit (PEL)
Indicates a high-voltage area of 600V or greater
Identifies an area with noise levels exceeding 85 dB
questions.correct_answer: Advises personnel of an RF hazard at the boundary of the Permissible Exposure Limit (PEL)

questions.question: What is the function of a Type 2 RADHAZ warning sign?
options: Advises personnel of an RF hazard at the boundary of the Permissible Exposure Limit (PEL)
Excludes personnel from proceeding past a designated point without checking with command authority
Warns of hazardous noise levels where portable music players are prohibited
Identifies the physical boundary of a Tag-Out isolation zone
questions.correct_answer: Excludes personnel from proceeding past a designated point without checking with command authority

questions.question: RF transmitters of what power rating and above can create severe RF-burn hazards due to complicated shipboard metallic structures?
options: 100 Watts and above
500 Watts and above
1 kilowatt (kW) and above
10 kilowatts (kW) and above
questions.correct_answer: 1 kilowatt (kW) and above

questions.question: In the Tag-Out System, what does a red DANGER tag indicate?
options: Prohibits operation of equipment that could jeopardize personnel safety or damage equipment
Provides temporary special operating instructions for a component
Indicates that an instrument is out of calibration
Marks a physical leak in a fluid boundary line
questions.correct_answer: Prohibits operation of equipment that could jeopardize personnel safety or damage equipment

questions.question: In the Tag-Out System, what is the purpose of a yellow CAUTION tag?
options: To completely prohibit the operation of a system under maintenance
To provide temporary special operating instructions or indicate unusual actions required to operate equipment
To identify that a component is permanently out of commission
To serve as a substitute for a missing lock on an electrical breaker
questions.correct_answer: To provide temporary special operating instructions or indicate unusual actions required to operate equipment

questions.question: What is the standard format for a tag-out serial number?
options: The ship's hull number followed by a sequential date
Department and division designators followed by a hyphen and a sequential number (e.g., ENG-DANGER-0001)
Technician initials followed by system name and time of day
The Work Authorization Form (WAF) number with a 'RED' or 'YELLOW' prefix
questions.correct_answer: Department and division designators followed by a hyphen and a sequential number (e.g., ENG-DANGER-0001)

questions.question: Under what shipboard weather or environmental conditions must personnel working aloft immediately stop work?
options: Winds exceed 20 km/h or ship rolls more than 5 degrees
Winds exceed 30 km/h or ship rolls more than 10 degrees
Winds exceed 40 km/h or ship rolls more than 15 degrees
Winds exceed 50 km/h or ship rolls more than 20 degrees
questions.correct_answer: Winds exceed 30 km/h or ship rolls more than 10 degrees

questions.question: Prior to personnel working aloft and every 15 minutes after, what verbal warning must be passed over the ship's 1MC?
options: "Personnel are working aloft. Do not rotate antennas, energize or radiate any electrical or electronic equipment while personnel are working aloft."
"Caution, secure all high-power transmitters due to mast maintenance in progress."
"Do not rotate radars or antennas without direct written permission from the safety observer aloft."
"Personnel aloft. Keep clear of the main deck and maintain silence on all radio circuits."
questions.correct_answer: "Personnel are working aloft. Do not rotate antennas, energize or radiate any electrical or electronic equipment while personnel are working aloft."

questions.question: What is the maximum voltage rating for Navy-issued electrical safety shoes designed to protect personnel with non-conducting soles?
Under the Navy Hearing Conservation Program (HCP), at what continuous noise level must personnel wear hearing protection, and what is prohibited in these zones?
options: Exceeds 75 dB; wearing safety glasses is prohibited
Exceeds 80 dB; speaking over sound-powered phones is prohibited
Exceeds 85 dB; wearing portable music players with headphones or earbuds is prohibited
Exceeds 90 dB; wearing commercial earmuffs is prohibited
questions.correct_answer: Exceeds 85 dB; wearing portable music players with headphones or earbuds is prohibited

questions.question: When working with paints, solvents, and cleaning materials for electrical equipment in unventilated spaces, what type of PPE is required?
options: An air-purifying respirator with adequate oxygen levels of 22% or more by volume
A standard cloth dust mask
A SCBA with less than 15% oxygen
Rubber insulating gloves of Class 3 only
questions.correct_answer: An air-purifying respirator with adequate oxygen levels of 22% or more by volume

questions.question: What physical constant describes the speed of electromagnetic waves in outer space?
options: 186,000 miles per second
300,000 miles per second
186,000 miles per minute
1,100 feet per second
questions.correct_answer: 186,000 miles per second

questions.question: Which atmospheric layer extends from the Earth's surface to about 6 to 10 miles and contains all weather conditions, such as clouds, that can affect space wave propagation?
options: Ionosphere
Stratosphere
Troposphere
Exosphere
questions.correct_answer: Troposphere

questions.question: Why does the stratosphere have relatively little effect on radio waves?
options: It consists entirely of ionized gases that absorb RF energy
It is too close to the Earth's surface to interact with waves
It has a relatively constant temperature with stable characteristics
It is completely devoid of any air molecules
questions.correct_answer: It has a relatively constant temperature with stable characteristics

questions.question: Which atmospheric layer, located 30 to 250 miles above the Earth's surface, is the most crucial for long-distance point-to-point (PTP) RF communications?
options: Troposphere
Stratosphere
Ionosphere
Thermosphere
questions.correct_answer: Ionosphere

questions.question: How does the sun affect RF communications through the ionosphere during daylight hours?
options: It stops all ionization, requiring lower frequencies
It causes less radiation, meaning radio waves escape into space
It increases ionization, requiring higher frequency waves to be used
It merges all layers into a single D layer
questions.correct_answer: It increases ionization, requiring higher frequency waves to be used

questions.question: What occurs in the ionospheric F layer during daylight hours?
options: It completely disappears due to extreme solar heat
It separates into two distinct sublayers, F1 and F2, due to ionization
It sinks to the level of the troposphere
It blocks all Extremely High Frequency (EHF) transmissions
questions.correct_answer: It separates into two distinct sublayers, F1 and F2, due to ionization

questions.question: Which radio propagation behavior describes waves bouncing off flat surfaces, potentially causing multi-path distortions?
options: Reflection
Refraction
Diffraction
Attenuation
questions.correct_answer: Reflection

questions.question: Which propagation behavior involves the bending of radio waves as they move between different media with varying temperature, pressure, humidity, or density?
options: Reflection
Refraction
Diffraction
Absorption
questions.correct_answer: Refraction

questions.question: What is diffraction in the context of radio wave propagation?
options: The loss of wave energy due to heat absorption by the ground
The splitting of a carrier wave into an audio signal and a data signal
The bending of radio waves around solid or dense objects, allowing communication despite obstacles
The phase shift that occurs when combining two amplitude modulated signals
questions.correct_answer: The bending of radio waves around solid or dense objects, allowing communication despite obstacles

questions.question: What does the Frequency of Optimum Transmission (FOT) represent in RF planning?
options: The lowest frequency that can be used for successful communication
The highest frequency that can be used before a signal escapes into space
The frequency that is most reliable for radio wave propagation, usable for 90% of the days of the month
The frequency reserved strictly for emergency distress calls
questions.correct_answer: The frequency that is most reliable for radio wave propagation, usable for 90% of the days of the month

questions.question: What is the term for the loss of energy in radio waves as they travel over the Earth's surface, causing a decrease in signal strength?
options: Refraction
Diffraction
Attenuation
Modulation
questions.correct_answer: Attenuation

questions.question: Which wave path travels directly from the transmit antenna to the receive antenna and is highly affected by atmospheric/weather conditions?
options: Surface Waves
Space Waves
Sky Waves
Indirect Waves
questions.correct_answer: Space Waves

questions.question: Which wave path involves waves that are transmitted into the atmosphere, refracted by the uppermost layer, and returned to the Earth's surface at greater distances?
options: Surface Waves
Space Waves
Sky Waves
Direct Waves
questions.correct_answer: Sky Waves

questions.question: What is the frequency range and primary military use of Extremely Low Frequency (ELF) waves?
options: 30-300 kHz; medium-range surface ship communications
Up to 3 kHz; one-way communications with submarines at depths of hundreds of feet over distances of 5000+ miles
3-30 MHz; long-range tactical voice and data circuits
30-300 MHz; Line-of-Sight local communications
questions.correct_answer: Up to 3 kHz; one-way communications with submarines at depths of hundreds of feet over distances of 5000+ miles

questions.question: What are the common uses of Very Low Frequency (VLF) waves in the Navy?
options: Short-range ship-to-ship tactical voice nets
One-way communications with submarines in shallow water and navigational systems over 5000+ miles
High-capacity commercial internet broadband services
Aegis BMD tracking and missile guidance data links
questions.correct_answer: One-way communications with submarines in shallow water and navigational systems over 5000+ miles

questions.question: What is the frequency range and distance coverage of Low Frequency (LF) waves?
options: Up to 3 kHz; over 5000 miles
30-300 kHz; 1000 to 5000 miles
3-30 MHz; up to 2000 miles
300 MHz to 3 GHz; 25-35 miles
questions.correct_answer: 30-300 kHz; 1000 to 5000 miles

questions.question: Which RF band operates in the 3-30 MHz range, covers distances up to 2,000 miles, and supports secure/unsecure voice and data circuits?
options: Low Frequency (LF)
Medium Frequency (MF)
High Frequency (HF)
Very High Frequency (VHF)
questions.correct_answer: High Frequency (HF)

questions.question: What is the typical range of Line-of-Sight (LOS) communications, such as those in the VHF and UHF bands?
options: 5 to 10 nautical miles
25 to 35 nautical miles
100 to 120 nautical miles
150 to 300 nautical miles
questions.correct_answer: 25 to 35 nautical miles

questions.question: On the RF spectrum, how do wavelength and energy levels change as you move from EHF to ELF?
options: Wavelength decreases, energy increases
Wavelength increases, energy decreases
Wavelength increases, energy increases
Wavelength decreases, energy decreases
questions.correct_answer: Wavelength increases, energy decreases

questions.question: On the RF spectrum, how do wavelength and energy levels change as you move from ELF to EHF?
options: Wavelength decreases, energy increases
Wavelength increases, energy decreases
Wavelength increases, energy increases
Wavelength decreases, energy decreases
questions.correct_answer: Wavelength decreases, energy increases

questions.question: What is one primary advantage of digital signals over analog signals?
options: They require less bandwidth and do not use electrical impulses
They are easily audible to the human ear without a receiver
They do not degrade over time; if the numbers can be read, the same wave is generated, making them easy to clean up and encrypt
They are completely unaffected by weather conditions in the troposphere
questions.correct_answer: They do not degrade over time; if the numbers can be read, the same wave is generated, making them easy to clean up and encrypt

questions.question: Which digital data transmission timing is low-speed, does not use an associated clock, and relies on start and stop bits?
options: Synchronous (SYNC)
Asynchronous (ASYNC)
Isochronous (ISOC)
Co-directional
questions.correct_answer: Asynchronous (ASYNC)

questions.question: What characterizes Isochronous (ISOC) data transmission?
options: Data is transmitted at a rate determined by an atomic cesium clock
Data is transmitted without an associated clock and without associated start and stop bits
Data is combined using Time Division Multiple Access
Data is transmitted in continuous, varying waves using analog switchboards
questions.correct_answer: Data is transmitted without an associated clock and without associated start and stop bits

questions.question: What is the difference between Co-directional and Counter-directional clocks in digital communications?
options: Co-directional clocks use GPS; Counter-directional clocks use rubidium standards
Co-directional clocks and data signals originate from the same source; Counter-directional clocks and data signals originate from opposite sources
Co-directional clocks are used for unclassified enclaves; Counter-directional are used for secret enclaves
Co-directional clocks flow over red patch panels; Counter-directional flow over black patch panels
questions.correct_answer: Co-directional clocks and data signals originate from the same source; Counter-directional clocks and data signals originate from opposite sources

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of signal conversion when a signal is received from a satellite?
options: RF -> AF -> IF
RF -> IF -> AF
AF -> IF -> RF
IF -> RF -> AF
questions.correct_answer: RF -> IF -> AF

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of signal conversion for a received data circuit?
options: RF -> IF -> DC
RF -> DC -> IF
DC -> IF -> RF
IF -> RF -> DC
questions.correct_answer: RF -> IF -> DC

questions.question: What is the range of human hearing, referred to as Audio Frequency (AF)?
options: 20 Hz to 20 kHz
3 kHz to 30 kHz
300 Hz to 3 GHz
100 kHz to 100 MHz
questions.correct_answer: 20 Hz to 20 kHz

questions.question: What does a Data Terminal Equipment (DTE) device do, and what is an example?
options: It accepts a signal for transmission; e.g., a modem
It generates an outgoing data signal; e.g., a computer terminal
It tunes antennas to specific frequencies; e.g., a coupler
It scrambles data for secure communications; e.g., cryptographic equipment
questions.correct_answer: It generates an outgoing data signal; e.g., a computer terminal

questions.question: What does a Data Communications Equipment (DCE) device do, and what is an example?
options: It generates an outgoing data signal; e.g., a computer terminal
It accepts a signal for transmission; e.g., a modem
It splits the F layer into F1 and F2; e.g., the sun
It switches analog interfaces; e.g., SA-2112(V)
questions.correct_answer: It accepts a signal for transmission; e.g., a modem

questions.question: What modulation technique combines two amplitude modulated signals into a single channel, differing in phase by 90 degrees, to allow high bandwidth speeds?
options: Frequency-Shift Keying (FSK)
Phase-Shift Keying (PSK)
Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM)
Phase Modulation (PM)
questions.correct_answer: Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM)

questions.question: What is the standard baud rate used by the Navy for Frequency-Shift Keying (FSK) with circuit data?
options: 75 bits per second (bps)
1200 bits per second (bps)
9600 bits per second (bps)
16 kilobits per second (kbps)
questions.correct_answer: 75 bits per second (bps)

questions.question: What does the Eb/No value measure in digital communications systems, and what occurs if it is too low?
options: Bandwidth utilization; when too low, the data rate drops slightly but connections remain stable
The Signal-to-Noise ratio (SNR); when too low, there is a tendency toward signal loss and increased fault indications
Atmospheric ionization; when too low, sky waves cannot refract
Cryptographic key synchronization; when too low, keys must be manually re-loaded
questions.correct_answer: The Signal-to-Noise ratio (SNR); when too low, there is a tendency toward signal loss and increased fault indications

questions.question: What is the most common patch panel used in Navy RF communications?
options: AN/USQ-155(V)

questions.question: In RF patching, what does a RED patch panel indicate, and what does a BLACK patch panel indicate?
options: RED is encrypted; BLACK is unsecure or decrypted
RED is unsecure/decrypted/unencrypted; BLACK is encrypted
RED is high-voltage; BLACK is low-voltage
RED is analog; BLACK is digital
questions.correct_answer: RED is unsecure/decrypted/unencrypted; BLACK is encrypted

questions.question: What is the SA-2112(V) Secure Audio Switch (SAS) housed in, and what is its specific limitation?
options: Housed in a black cabinet; limited to switching digital data only
Housed in a bright red cabinet; limited to connecting crypto interface units in voice circuits only
Housed in a yellow cabinet; limited to switching UHF DAMA circuits only
Housed in a steel vault; limited to strategic command networks only
questions.correct_answer: Housed in a bright red cabinet; limited to connecting crypto interface units in voice circuits only

questions.question: What are the characteristics of Ultra-High Frequency (UHF) SATCOM?
options: High capacity, low mobility, moderate anti-jam
High capacity, moderate mobility, high anti-jam
Low capacity, high mobility, low anti-jam, and vulnerable to nuclear radiation
Low capacity, low mobility, high anti-jam
questions.correct_answer: Low capacity, high mobility, low anti-jam, and vulnerable to nuclear radiation

questions.question: What is the maximum data transmission speed of Super High Frequency (SHF) SATCOM?
options: Up to 2.048 Mbps
Up to 8.192 Mbps
Up to 21.6 Mbps
Up to 155 Megabits per second (Mbps)
questions.correct_answer: Up to 155 Megabits per second (Mbps)

questions.question: Which satellite orbit is found at approximately 22,500 miles and travels at the exact same rate as the Earth's rotation?
options: Low Earth Orbit (LEO)
Medium Earth Orbit (MEO)
Highly Elliptical Orbit (HEO) / Molniya
Geosynchronous Orbit
questions.correct_answer: Geosynchronous Orbit

Waves transmitted into the atmosphere that are refracted by the ionosphere and return to the Earth's surface at greater distances.
